title: Dedicated autoscaler: handle region capacity shortage when min bound cannot be met
author: Keiko Yamamoto
description:
Context: With min/max bounds enabled for Dedicated, the autoscaler must never *request* less than min, but in practice the fleet may be unable to *provision* the requested min due to regional GPU shortages (insufficient capacity, placement failures, or temporary allocator degradation). Prior behavior was ambiguous: the loop would repeatedly attempt to reach min every tick, spamming allocator calls/events and leaving customers/SRE without a deterministic surfaced state.

This PR adds explicit handling for "min bound unmet" scenarios:
- Surfaces a degraded capacity condition on the deployment when min cannot be provisioned, including reason + last allocator error (sanitized) and an estimate of missing replicas.
- Adds backoff/jitter on repeated provisioning attempts when the failure reason indicates regional shortage, to prevent thundering herd and noisy logs.
- Emits metrics and structured logs so SRE can alert on sustained unmet-min and so Console can display a clear "Degraded (min unmet)" status.

Behavioral semantics (aligned with ADR draft + ENG-22151):
- Hard invariant remains: desired capacity is clamped to [min, max] *as a policy decision*.
- If allocator cannot satisfy min, we record two values: policy_desired_replicas=min (bounded desired), provisioned_replicas=<actual>, and we mark the deployment as Degraded with condition MIN_CAPACITY_UNMET.
- Reactive signals still influence policy_desired within bounds, but they cannot hide the fact that min is not currently achievable.
- Once provisioning recovers (allocator starts returning capacity), the degraded condition automatically clears after N consecutive successful ticks.

Implementation summary:
1) Autoscaler loop: detect shortage-class errors from FleetAllocator (InsufficientCapacity, PlacementUnavailable, RegionUnavailable).
2) Backoff: per-deployment exponential backoff (min 15s, max 10m) with +/-20% jitter, only applied for shortage-class failures; non-shortage failures continue to retry each tick (to catch transient bugs quickly).
3) Status propagation: extend internal CapacityStatus payload with `min_target_replicas`, `min_unmet_replicas`, `min_unmet_since`, `shortage_reason` and `last_shortage_error_code`. This is emitted to the control plane status writer used by Console.
4) Observability: new counters/gauges + structured event "dedicated_autoscaler_min_unmet" with reason and bounded/provisioned values. (Alert rules are in a separate observability-pack PR; this PR provides the signals.)

Testing:
- Unit tests for shortage classification + backoff behavior.
- Integration-ish test using fake allocator: simulate sustained shortage then recovery, verify condition set/cleared and that allocator call rate drops under backoff.
- Golden log snapshot for auditability of the decision record: requested_desired, bounded_desired, provisioned, reason.

Rollout notes:
- Code paths are gated behind the existing bounds feature flag; for accounts without bounds enabled, no behavior change.
- The degraded condition is additive; it will appear in internal admin tooling immediately, and Console will surface it once the UI reads the new status fields.

Follow-ups:
- Hook this condition into Smart Routing signals (so routing can degrade gracefully when min is unmet) is tracked separately.
- SRE alert thresholds and runbook links: see ENG-22145 / dedicated-autoscaler troubleshooting runbook updates.

Refs: ENG-22151, SUP-28452, discussion in eng-sre about shortage visibility and paging noise.
commits: autoscaler: classify allocator errors as shortage vs transient
autoscaler: add per-deployment backoff + jitter for shortage retry loop
control-plane status: include min target/unmet fields in capacity status
observability: emit min_unmet metrics + structured logs
notable_snippets: Added MIN_CAPACITY_UNMET condition emission: condition is set when provisioned_replicas < min_target_replicas AND last error is shortage-class; clears after 3 consecutive successful reconciles with provisioned >= min_target.
Backoff key is (deployment_id, region). Backoff only applies to allocator Provision() calls; status writing still happens every tick to keep timestamps fresh.
review_conversation:
Vanessa Ortiz (review): Can we confirm we’re not accidentally suppressing retries for non-shortage allocator errors (e.g., auth, bad request)?
Keiko Yamamoto (author): Yep — backoff is only applied for InsufficientCapacity/PlacementUnavailable/RegionUnavailable. Everything else retries per tick and increments `dedicated_autoscaler_provision_error_total{class="non_shortage"}`.

Rafael Mendes (review): Please add explicit "unmet since" timestamp so on-call can correlate to regional incidents, and ensure logs are rate-limited.
Keiko Yamamoto (author): Added `min_unmet_since` in status + structured log emitted only on state transitions (healthy->unmet, unmet->healthy) and once every 10m while unmet.

Allison Grant (review): Metric naming: align with metric naming standards (no high-card labels, keep reason as low-card enum). Also add a gauge for unmet replicas.
Keiko Yamamoto (author): Updated metrics to `dedicated_autoscaler_min_unmet_replicas` (gauge) and `dedicated_autoscaler_min_unmet_total` (counter) with `reason_code` as an enum; no raw error strings in labels.

Jordan Lee (review): Status schema change — is this backwards compatible for old Console? Make sure default/empty values won’t break parsing.
Keiko Yamamoto (author): Fields are additive and optional; writer populates zero values when missing. Console backend ignores unknown fields; UI update will come later.

Vanessa Ortiz (approval): Looks good after the backoff jitter + transition-only logging changes. Ship it behind the bounds flag.
Rafael Mendes (approval): Approved with the condition clear hysteresis; please link the runbook in the follow-up PR.
Allison Grant (approval): Approved once metrics names updated.
release_notes: Internal: Dedicated autoscaler now surfaces a Degraded condition when regional GPU shortages prevent meeting configured min capacity, with retry backoff and new observability signals (behind bounds feature flag).
